key_insight: A semi-automated, expert-guided annotation workflow can make intraoperative neurosurgical ultrasound labeling much faster and more scalable for AI development.
clinical_relevance: If validated further, this approach could help build the annotated ultrasound datasets needed for future real-time brain tumor and anatomy AI tools in surgery.
method: Napari-based interactive labeling with a scikit-learn Random Forest pixel classifier
Sparse expert brush annotations on representative intraoperative ultrasound frames from five craniotomy cases
Features included raw intensity, multi-scale Gaussian filtering, Laplacian of Gaussian, and Sobel edge magnitude
evidence_signal: In five intraoperative cases, sparse annotations were enough to train case-specific models that propagated labels across full video sequences, with out-of-bag validation and probability maps used to assess uncertainty.
watch_item: This is a proof-of-concept on a very small, case-specific dataset, so generalization and real-world robustness remain unproven.
paper_title: A Semi-Automated Interactive Annotation Framework for Intraoperative Neurosurgical Ultrasound: A Proof-of-Concept Study
